sam: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selection change I see a 7-12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for 2 long-running customers. :frowning:
marie: oof. same machines/seq dist?
sam: Same Ampere fleet, seq distribution unchanged. The profiler points at more KV cache churn and slightly different batch packing (fewer same-prefix coalesces).
lee: do you have traces? can we repro locally with the old kernels vs new?
sam: repro is flaky but captured one trace. main observations:
- streaming requests that hit client-side retry path end up with different `X-Redwood-Cache` headers, which means different cache keys
- kernel change altered small-padding behavior, so batching heuristics split a few requests earlier
- KV cache warmup (on-demand) is slower with the new packing, TTLs not being refreshed on retry flow

sam: log snippet:```
[2026-03-14T09:12:11Z] req id=abc123 header X-Redwood-Cache=opt-in-v2 prefix_key=usr:42:ctx:sha256:deadbeef
[2026-03-14T09:12:11Z] retry path: set header X-Redwood-Cache=opt-in
[2026-03-14T09:12:11Z] cache miss (expected hit) key_mismatch=true
```
marie: interesting — header canonicalization bug? we normalize header values in runtime but SDK was changed to allow `opt-in-v2` for experiments. maybe runtime only understands `opt-in`.
alex: iirc we fold variants in kernel selection to prefer combiner-friendly packing, but that can change token offsets used in the prefix hashing. maybe kernel pad changed from 8->16 which shifts batch boundaries.
lee: for a short mitigation we can accept both header variants in cache key canonicalizer and add a compatibility mapping in the runtime. also add a telemetry gauge for "cache_header_variant" to quantify impact.
marie: agree. also let's add a small change to SDK to make retries preserve canonical header exactly (no experimental suffix). PR ready?
sam: putting up a small repro + fix for header canonicalization in runtime + SDK note. Also we should add an integration test: simulate streaming retry by failing chunk 1 -> retry -> ensure header preserved and cache key stable.
perf-bot: perf-regression alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate down 9% over 12h (p95 latency +3ms). Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/alerts/1918765432
alex: can we also instrument batch composition: emit batch_signature=(kernel, pad, seq_len_buckets, first_token_index) and tag cache keys with batch_signature during logs. will help correlate kernel selection -> cache misses.
sam: good idea — I'll add batch_signature and a short sampling rate. low overhead.
lee: timeline: sam + marie will push header canonicalizer + SDK note today; alex will add batch_signature telemetry; sam will enable compatibility mapping as temporary fallback. we'll monitor hit-rate and roll kernel selection back if not fixed by EOD. :thumbsup:
marie: filed followups: #1 SDK retry header deterministic flag; #2 runtime cache key canonicalizer mapping; #3 test for streaming retry path.
sam: thanks. leaving thread with repro link and logs in the ticket.
